$comment: P15 — the performance budget, asserted rather than admired.
HANDOFF records an honest gap: the P12 font work is structurally verified —
zero external origins is not a matter of measurement — but its effect on LCP
was never independently confirmed, because PageSpeed Insights rate-limited
every attempt from that network. This is the fix for that: the number gets
measured on every run instead of being asked for once and never again.
Three runs per URL because Lighthouse's own variance on a shared CI runner is
several points; a single run would fail the build on noise. The median is what
is asserted.
The categories are thresholds, not aspirations. Accessibility and best
practices are pinned at 1.0 because both are pass/fail checklists where a
miss is a real defect — and because axe already covers accessibility in the
E2E suite, so a Lighthouse a11y regression means something the E2E excluded.
-- WHY THE PER-ASSERTION NOTES LIVE UP HERE --
Do NOT put explanatory keys inside `assert.assertions`. Every key in that
object is read as an AUDIT NAME, so a `$comment-lcp` key becomes an assertion
against an audit that does not exist and fails with '"$comment-lcp" is not a
known audit'. Four such comments once produced twelve spurious failures — four
per URL across three URLs — which is most of what made this job look broken.
This top-level `$comment` key is ignored by lhci, so notes are safe here.
cumulative-layout-shift: 0 today, and the metric the vendored fonts'
size-adjust fallback exists to protect. A regression here means the fallback
metrics stopped matching.
largest-contentful-paint: the number P12 was aiming at and never got to
confirm.
unused-css-rules / uses-long-cache-ttl: render-blocking CSS went 114.6KB ->
96.2KB when the route-scoped stylesheets were split out. This is the guard
that stops it creeping back.
third-party-summary: vendored in P12. A third-party font origin reappearing is
the exact regression that broke the build.
